We have Original Question, Task Skeleton fixed. Need assign statuses. Claims:
C1 Jerry Mao Australian competitive programmer, IOI medals sequence bronze 2015, silver 2016, gold 2017, silver 2018.
C2 Jerry Mao member of MIT team MIT ZEROONE (with Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao), which won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022) as World Champion.

Requirements:
R1 Annual university programming final: Every year teams of competitive programmers from universities around world compete in final of prestigious programming contest for prestigious title. Is this supported? Claims mention ICPC 2021 World Finals, team MIT ZEROONE won as World Champion. Does that establish annual university programming final? Partially maybe: C2 establishes a team from MIT (university) won ICPC World Finals, which is a prestigious programming contest final. But "every year, teams from universities around world compete" is background/general. Claim C2 establishes one instance? Need status. It may support existence of such contest in a year, with university team. But not necessarily annual/every year. The requirement is a general claim. It may be partially supported by C2 (university team competed and won final of prestigious contest) but annual/every year not established. Is "prestigious programming contest" ICPC? C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka, World Champion. It doesn't explicitly say "prestigious" or "every year", "teams from universities around world". It mentions MIT team. Could be partial. Need exactly one. We'll decide later.

R2 Winning team and Australian coder: In one particular year, a team featuring an Australian coder won championship. C1 says Jerry Mao is Australian competitive programmer. C2 says Jerry Mao was member of MIT ZEROONE, which won ICPC 2021 World Finals as World Champion. Together fully support: team featuring Australian coder won championship. Yes fully_supported (for ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka? The championship). Note C2 has team with Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. Jerry Mao Australian. So R2 fully.

R3 Coder medal sequence: secured bronze, silver, gold, and another silver in four consecutive IOIs. C1 exactly states bronze IOI 2015, silver 2016, gold 2017, silver 2018. Four consecutive IOIs. Fully_supported C1.

R4 Other teammates country relation: His other two teammates were from same country. Claims: C2 says teammates were Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. Does it say they were from same country? It says team MIT ZEROONE with Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. MIT is in USA? Names may suggest Chinese? But no explicit country. C1 says Jerry Mao Australian. No claim establishes other two teammates' country, or same country as each other / as him. "same country" refers to Australian coder? In original: "His other two teammates were from the same country." Same country likely as him? Wait wording: "His other two teammates were from the same country." Could mean same country as the Australian coder? Actually if coder is Australian, his other two teammates were from same country (Australia?) But C2 says teammates Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao, likely not Australian. Hmm task skeleton R4 label: "Other teammates country relation", source: "His other two teammates were from the same country." It doesn't specify same as him? It says same country. Need evaluate based on claims. Claims only name teammates, no country. So unsupported. supported_by empty.

R5 Requested winning year: Could you tell me the year associated with competition title. C2 states ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022) as World Champion. What is "year associated with competition title"? The contest is ICPC 2021 World Finals, held in 2022. The team won championship. The question asks year associated with competition title. In ICPC, "2021 World Finals" might be year associated with title. C2 provides "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022)". Does that establish the year? Yes, could be 2021 (title year) or 2022 held date. The requirement is "year associated with the competition title". C2 gives both 2021 in title and 2022 held. It supports that the winning year was 2021? Need be careful. The original question asks "the year associated with the competition title" likely the competition year (ICPC 2021). C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka. So fully_supported? It provides year 2021 associated with title. It also says held on 10 Nov 2022. But requirement: requested winning year. C2 says won ICPC 2021 World Finals. Thus year associated with title is 2021. Fully supported by C2. But maybe the final was held in 2022; question wording "year associated with the competition title" ambiguous but Claim gives both. I'd mark fully_supported for "year associated with competition title" because C2 states ICPC 2021 World Finals. If asks "the year he won that title" maybe 2021? Yes.

R6 Requested host university: name of host university for the year he won that title. C2 says World Finals Dhaka. Dhaka is a city, not university. It mentions MIT team, not host university. Does not establish host university. So unsupported. supported_by empty. Unless MIT is team's university, not host. The host university of ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka? I happen to know might be University of Dhaka? But no outside knowledge; claim doesn't say. So unsupported.

R1: Need decide. Claim C2 says "Massachusetts Institute of Technology team MIT ZEROONE ... won the ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka ... as World Champion." Does this establish R1: "Every year, teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world compete in the final of a prestigious programming contest for the prestigious title." This is a general annual contest. Claim C2 establishes an ICPC World Finals event, a team from MIT, World Champion. It implies a university team competed in final of a programming contest, won title. But not "every year" nor "from universities around the world" (plural? at least MIT). It doesn't mention other university teams around the world. Could be partial? The requirement has multiple material parts:
- Every year
- teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world
- compete in final
- prestigious programming contest
- for prestigious title.

C2 establishes at least: a team from MIT (university) competed in ICPC World Finals and won as World Champion. This is a final of a programming contest and title. It does not establish "every year" or "around the world" or "prestigious" explicitly? "ICPC World Finals" and "World Champion" imply prestige? But outside? Maybe "World Finals" is a contest final; "World Champion" title. The claim itself says won "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka ... as World Champion." This establishes there is a programming contest final and a championship title. It doesn't say prestigious. The requirement includes "prestigious programming contest" but that's evaluative. C2's "World Finals" and "World Champion" may imply prestigious? We should avoid outside. It is descriptive.

For partial_supported, need at least one substantive material part. C2 supports that a university team competed in/won a world finals programming contest. That's substantive part of R1. It does not support every year or around the world. So partially_supported. Supported_by C2. Could C1 not relevant to R1. So R1 partially_supported with C2.

But let's examine if R1 could be fully_supported? No, no annual/general. So partial.

R2 fully C1,C2. R3 fully C1. R4 unsupported. R5 fully C2. R6 unsupported. Need JSON.

Need ensure supported_by arrays contain claim IDs only. For unsupported empty.

Let's craft final JSON.

Need no extra. Ensure valid JSON schema exactly. 
{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C2"]},...]} 
For R2 fully_supported supported_by ["C1","C2"]. Is C1 needed? C2 alone says Jerry Mao member, but doesn't say Australian. C1 provides Australian. So both. R3 C1. R5 C2. R6 unsupported empty. R4 unsupported empty.

Check R5: Could "year associated with competition title" be 2021. C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held 10 Nov 2022). Does it establish the year he won that title? It says won as World Champion. Yes. If they ask "year associated with competition title" maybe 2021, fully. Good.

Potential issue: R2 "In one particular year, I discovered that a team featuring an Australian coder won the championship." C2 says team MIT ZEROONE won ICPC 2021 World Finals as World Champion. C1 says Jerry Mao Australian. Yes.

Potential issue R1: The claim C2 supports that MIT team won ICPC 2021 World Finals. Does that establish "teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world compete in the final" for that year? It mentions one team from MIT. Not "around the world", but the event is World Finals. It might be partial. Good.

Potential issue R4: "His other two teammates were from the same country." C2 names teammates Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. It does not say country. Could names imply Chinese? No outside. Unsupported.

R6: C2 mentions "Dhaka" but not host university. Unsupported.
